title: Galley proof
intro: In printing and publishing, proofs are the preliminary versions of publications meant for review by authors, editors, and proofreaders, often with extra-wide margins. Galley proofs may be uncut and unbound, or in some cases electronically transmitted.

title: Garden of Eden (cellular automaton)
intro: In a cellular automaton, a Garden of Eden is a configuration that has no predecessor. It can be the initial configuration of the automaton but cannot arise in any other way.

title: Gauss–Legendre algorithm
intro: The Gauss–Legendre algorithm is an algorithm to compute the digits of π. It is notable for being rapidly convergent, with only 25 iterations producing 45 million correct digits of π.

title: Gauss–Lucas theorem
intro: In complex analysis, a branch of mathematics, the Gauss–Lucas theorem gives a geometric relation between the roots of a polynomial P and the roots of its derivative P′. The set of roots of a real or complex polynomial is a set of points in the complex plane.

title: Gauss–Markov theorem
intro: In statistics, the Gauss–Markov theorem (or simply Gauss theorem for some authors) states that, under certain conditions, the ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator for linear regression has the lowest variance among all linear unbiased estimators. The theorem guarantees that OLS is the most precise way to estimate regression coefficients within that class of estimation methods.

title: Gauss's lemma (number theory)
intro: Gauss's lemma in number theory gives a condition for an integer to be a quadratic residue. Although it is not useful computationally, it has theoretical significance, being involved in some proofs of quadratic reciprocity.
